newsitem.title: UK: Austria to set 5.0 bln Ffr bond Monday afternoon.
newsitem.headline: Austria to set 5.0 bln Ffr bond Monday afternoon.

text.p: Austria will launch a 5.0 billion French franc Eurobond due January 18, 2004 at a spread of seven basis points over OATs this afternoon, joint lead managers CDC and J.P. Morgan said on Monday.
The deal was expected at 1315 GMT and the spread was over the interpolated curve between the 6.75 percent OAT due October 2003 and the 8.25 percent OAT due February 2004.
The Austrian bond will carry a 5.50 percent coupon and have a January 18, 2004 maturity, exactly matching the details on an existing Austrian government schilling bond.
Holders of the franc bond will have an option to exchange their bonds for the Austrian bund.
Austria will have an option to redenominate the franc bond in euros after France joins the single European currency.

Austria may issue further bonds with a 5.50 percent coupon and January 2004 maturity in other core EMU currencies which it may also redenominate into euros. These further core EMU currency Austrian bonds may also be exchanged for the Austrian bund by investors.
Austria will have an option to consolidate bonds from these issues which are not exchanged into one jumbo euro Eurobond.
The ultimate aim is to have either a "super liquid Austrian euro Bund or a super liquid euro Eurobond" one banker said.
